title: Fuel regulator for gas engines
description: a fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines
reference_excerpt: The product in question is an N-LPR series regulator designed specifically for gaseous-fueled engines. It functions as a self-operating valve that utilizes engine vacuum to control the flow of fuel to the engine. The classification under HTSUS 8481.80.9015 is appropriate as it pertains to regulator valves that are self-operating and are used for controlling variables such as temperature, pressure, flow, and liquid level. The ruling confirms that this specific type of regulator falls under the category of self-operating valves, thus justifying the assigned HTS code.

classification.rationale: A fuel regulator dedicated to delivering gaseous fuel to an internal combustion engine is, per Section XVI Note 2, classified as a part of that engine under heading 8409 rather than as a generic valve of heading 8481, and CROSS precedent (H262289) confirms CBP treats CNG pressure regulators as fuel-system parts rather than stand-alone valves. However, without confirming whether the end product is a motor-vehicle part (which would instead fall under heading 8708 per Section XVII) or whether the engine is spark- or compression-ignition, the exact 8-10 digit line cannot be certain, so the best-guess statistical line 8409.91.99.90 is offered with low confidence pending clarification.
